pages.name: Quick Reference
pages.html:
The Nail is not a weapon and it never becomes one. Its whole progression is about turning Kattal's Strength into other people's survival.

Rod, legacy item (requires attunement by Kattal)

Your Charges

The Bastion Charges pool grows on its own at 6th, 10th and 15th level. You never have to update the sheet — the number just changes.

StateYour levelBastion ChargesBack at dawn
Dormantlevels 3–53all of them
Awakenedlevels 6–95all of them
Exaltedlevels 10–1471d6 + 1
Legendarylevel 15+91d8 + 1

At Dormant and Awakened every spent charge comes back. From 10th level it stops refilling completely: the pool is bigger, and a heavy day stays expensive into the next one.

Legacy Save DC

Where a feature makes something roll a saving throw, the DC is 8 + proficiency bonus + Strength modifier. It comes off your sheet, so it rises as you do.

What Unlocks When

Features arrive on their own. Below its level a feature is not on the item at all, so anything you can see on the sheet is something you can use. Where a later state improves an earlier feature, the old version disappears and the new one takes its place.

Dormant — levels 3–5 (Uncommon): Immovable Rod; Brace; Catch Them.

Awakened — levels 6–9 (Rare): Behind Me; No.; Carry the Impossible.

Exalted — levels 10–14 (Very Rare): You Go Through Me; Hold It!; Living Rampart.

Legendary — level 15+ (Legendary): The Unmoving; I Said No; The Last Wall.

Advancing

Reaching the level makes the next state possible. What actually wakes the item is the moment named at the top of each state below — a choice, not an achievement, and never something you can win in a fight. You do not need to chase it. When it happens, you will know, and so will the item.

pages.name: Levels 3–5 — Dormant
pages.html:
Uncommon · levels 3–5 · 3 Bastion Charges, all of them restored at dawn

Where it starts. This is the item as you first receive it. Everything below is yours from the moment you attune.

Everything from earlier states still works unless a feature here says it replaces one.

Immovable Rod

Press the Button. Action — no cost

The Nail retains the normal properties of an immovable rod. You can use an action to press the button, fixing the Nail in place until you or another creature uses an action to press the button again. It can hold up to 8,000 pounds; more weight causes it to deactivate and fall. A creature can use an action to make a DC 30 Strength check, moving the fixed Nail up to 10 feet on a success.

Brace

Passive. Always on while the conditions below are met. Nothing to spend.

While Kattal is holding the activated Rod, he has advantage on checks and saves against being knocked prone, reduces forced movement against himself by 10 feet, and has advantage on Strength checks made to lift, hold, push or prevent something from moving.

Catch Them

Reaction — 1 charge — STR or DEX save vs Legacy DC

When a creature within Kattal's reach falls, is knocked prone or is forcibly moved, he can use his reaction and expend 1 charge. A willing creature is automatically caught. An unwilling creature makes a Strength or Dexterity saving throw against Kattal's Legacy Save DC; on a failure he catches it. A falling creature stops falling if Kattal is capable of supporting its weight.

pages.name: Levels 6–9 — Awakened
pages.html:
Rare · levels 6–9 · 5 Bastion Charges, all of them restored at dawn

What wakes it. Kattal holds something dangerous back, or supports something failing, when releasing it would be safer for him.

Everything from earlier states still works unless a feature here says it replaces one.

Behind Me

Bonus action — 1 charge

As a bonus action, Kattal expends 1 charge and designates a creature within 5 feet. Until the beginning of his next turn, that creature gains half cover while it remains within 5 feet of him.

No.

No action — 2 charges

When Kattal fails a Strength check or Strength saving throw, he can expend 2 charges to treat the d20 as a 15.

Carry the Impossible

Passive. Always on, handled by an effect on the item. Nothing to click.

Kattal counts as two sizes larger when determining carrying capacity and how much weight he can push, drag or lift.

pages.name: Levels 10–14 — Exalted
pages.html:
Very Rare · levels 10–14 · 7 Bastion Charges, regaining 1d6 + 1 at dawn

What wakes it. Kattal deliberately makes himself the barrier between overwhelming danger and creatures unable to withstand it.

Everything from earlier states still works unless a feature here says it replaces one.

You Go Through Me

Bonus action — 3 charges — 1 minute

As a bonus action, Kattal can expend 3 charges to enter Bastion Stance for 1 minute. While in this stance:

  • Kattal cannot be forcibly moved or knocked prone while conscious unless he chooses;
  • allies within 5 feet gain half cover;
  • hostile creatures treat the area within 10 feet of Kattal as difficult terrain;
  • when a creature within Kattal's reach attacks an ally, Kattal can use his reaction to make one melee weapon attack against that creature.

The stance ends early if Kattal becomes incapacitated.

Hold It!

Hold It!. Reaction — no cost — contested check

Hold It! (Gargantuan). Reaction — 1 charge — contested check

When a Huge or smaller creature attempts to move through Kattal's reach, he can use his reaction to make an Athletics check contested by its Athletics or Acrobatics. On a success its speed becomes 0 for the remainder of the turn. He may attempt this against a Gargantuan creature by expending 1 Bastion Charge.

Living Rampart

No action — no cost

When Kattal would provide half cover to an ally, he may choose to provide three-quarters cover instead. Until the beginning of his next turn, attacks that miss that ally specifically because of this cover bonus hit Kattal instead if the attack roll would hit his AC.

pages.name: Level 15+ — Legendary
pages.html:
Legendary · level 15+ · 9 Bastion Charges, regaining 1d8 + 1 at dawn

What wakes it. Kattal stands against something he cannot reasonably overpower because someone behind him needs him to remain standing.

Everything from earlier states still works unless a feature here says it replaces one.

The Unmoving

Passive. Always on. Nothing to click and nothing to spend.

While conscious and touching the ground, Kattal cannot be forcibly moved or knocked prone unless he chooses, has advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws, and counts as Gargantuan solely for carrying, pushing, dragging, lifting and determining what creatures he can grapple or physically impede. He does not gain Gargantuan reach, weapon damage or occupied space.

I Said No

No action — 1× per short or long rest

Once per short or long rest, when Kattal fails a Strength saving throw or Strength check, he can choose to succeed instead. If the effect would move, crush, drag or physically overwhelm him, he may additionally prevent that effect from moving through his space until the beginning of his next turn.

The Last Wall

Bonus action — 1× per long rest — 1 minute

Once per long rest, as a bonus action, Kattal activates the Nail for 1 minute. He gains resistance to all damage, a 10-foot aura granting allies half cover, immunity to forced movement and prone, and one additional reaction each round that can only be used for Catch Them, Hold It!, Living Rampart or an opportunity attack. However, Kattal's speed becomes 0. He may end the effect at the beginning of any of his turns. He becomes exactly what the Nail has been teaching him to become since level 3: not the strongest creature on the battlefield, but the thing the battlefield cannot move.

pages.name: Playing It Well
pages.html:
The Nail is not a weapon and it never becomes one. Its whole progression is about turning Kattal's Strength into other people's survival.

At the Table

  • Catch Them has no save against a willing creature. Standing next to whoever is about to be thrown, dropped or knocked down is the entire build.
  • Brace only works while the Rod is activated. Press the button first; it is an action, and forgetting it is the most common way to lose the feature.
  • Hold It! is free against anything Huge or smaller. No charge, repeatable, contested check — it is the best crowd control he has and it costs nothing.
  • Living Rampart means taking the hit on purpose. Check his own hit points before offering the three-quarters cover.
  • The Last Wall sets his speed to 0. Choose the square before he uses it, because he is not leaving it for a minute.

Questions That Come Up

Does Carry the Impossible need switching on?
No. It reads his level by itself — four times capacity from 6th and eight times from 15th.

Can Catch Them stop a falling ally taking damage?
It stops the fall if he can support the weight, so the rest of the fall does no damage. Anything already fallen has already happened.

Does The Unmoving actually make him Gargantuan?
Only for carrying, pushing, dragging, lifting and deciding what he can grapple or physically block. Not reach, not weapon damage, not the space he occupies.

Can he use Hold It! and an opportunity attack in the same round?
Not normally — that is one reaction. During The Last Wall he gets a second reaction for exactly these.

Is the Nail a magic weapon he can hit people with?
No. It is a rod. Nothing on it improves an attack, and that is deliberate.

If Something Here Disagrees With the Item

The item on your sheet is the rules. This journal is generated from the same source, so the two should never differ — but if they do, the item wins and your DM should know.
